subject: maths
title: Year 9 Maths summary and memory tips

scenes.heading: Year 9 Maths summary and memory tips
scenes.sub: The whole year in two minutes
scenes.say: Eleven chapters, one quick tour. Here are the rules you must know from Year 9 Maths, and the memory tricks that make them stick.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A key ring: a few keys open every door in the house
scenes.science: A few core rules unlock almost every Year 9 question
scenes.breaks: A key fits one lock. A maths rule only works if you check the conditions, like a right angle for Pythagoras.
scenes.say: Think of a key ring. A handful of keys opens every door in the house. Year 9 is the same: a few core rules unlock almost every question. But unlike a key, a rule only works when its conditions are true, like needing a right angle for Pythagoras.

scenes.heading: Number, money and algebra
scenes.say: Simple interest adds the same amount every year. Compound interest multiplies by one plus r each year. When you multiply or divide an inequality by a negative, flip it. A negative index means one over, and anything to the power zero is one. When you expand two brackets, every term meets every term.
scenes.caption: Simple interest adds the same amount every year. Compound interest multiplies by (1 + r) each year. Multiply or divide an inequality by a negative? Flip it. a⁻ⁿ = 1/aⁿ and a⁰ = 1. Expanding two brackets: every term meets every term.

scenes.heading: SOH CAH TOA
notes: Label O, A, H from the angle
x is opposite 30°, 10 is the hypotenuse
scenes.say: First the triangle, then the thirty degree angle. From that angle, x is opposite and ten centimetres is the hypotenuse. Opposite and hypotenuse means sine. So x is ten times sine thirty degrees, which is five centimetres. Label the sides before you choose.
scenes.caption: From the 30° angle, x is opposite and 10 cm is the hypotenuse. O and H means sin. So x = 10 × sin 30° = 5 cm. Label the sides before you choose.

scenes.heading: Straight lines
scenes.say: Every straight line is y equals m x plus c. m is the gradient, rise over run: m for mountain. c is where it crosses the y-axis: c for crossing. Parallel lines share the same gradient. For perpendicular, flip and negate: two becomes negative one half.
scenes.caption: Every straight line is y = mx + c. m is the gradient, rise ÷ run: m for mountain. c is where it crosses the y-axis: c for crossing. Parallel: same gradient. Perpendicular: flip and negate, so 2 becomes −½.

scenes.heading: Parabolas
scenes.say: Here's y equals x squared minus four. First the curve, then the key points. The minus four moves the turning point down to zero, negative four. It crosses the x-axis where x squared is four: at negative two and two.
scenes.caption: Here's y = x² − 4. The − 4 moves the turning point down to (0, −4). It crosses the x-axis where x² = 4: at −2 and 2.

scenes.heading: Two rules people forget
scenes.say: Two rules people forget. With similar shapes, lengths multiply by the scale factor, but areas multiply by its square. On tree diagrams, multiply along the branches and add between them. And without replacement, the second set of probabilities changes.

points: y = mx + c: m mountain, c crossing
Halve and keep the sign swap
scenes.say: Quick recap. Compound interest multiplies. Pythagoras: longest side, add; shorter side, subtract. Label, then SOH CAH TOA, in degree mode. y equals m x plus c. And for algorithms, halve the interval and keep the sign swap. Now try the practice questions!
